description_full: Business First Bancshares, Inc. operates as the bank holding company for b1BANK that provides various banking products and services in Louisiana and Texas. It offers various deposit products and services, including checking and savings, time, and money market accounts; and certificates of deposits, remote deposit capture, and direct deposit services. The company also provides commercial and industrial loans, such as working capital, term, equipment financing, asset acquisition, expansion and development, borrowing base, and other loan products, as well as commercial lines of credit, accounts receivable factoring, agricultural financing, and letters of credit; construction and development loans; commercial real estate loans; residential real estate loans comprising first and second lien 1-4 family mortgage loans, and home equity lines of credit; and consumer loans, including secured and unsecured installment, and term loans. In addition, it offers wealth management products, including mutual funds, annuities, individual retirement accounts, and other financial products, as well as other fiduciary and private banking products and services. Further, the company provides a range of other financial services comprising debit and credit cards, treasury and cash management, merchant, automated clearing house, lock-box, receivables factoring, correspondent banking, and other treasury services, as well as employee and payroll benefits solutions; and drive-through banking facilities, automated teller machines, night depository, personalized checks, electronic funds transfer, domestic and foreign wire transfer, traveler's checks, vault, loan and deposit sweep accounts, interest-rate swaps, small business administration products, online and mobile banking, e-statements, and bank-by-mail services. Business First Bancshares, Inc. was incorporated in 2006 and is headquartered in Baton Rouge, Louisiana.

financial_summary: Business First Bancshares, Inc. is a small-cap financial services business with a $1.0B market cap on $325M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +12% over the past three years and +24% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 17% against a 9% cost of capital, a 8-point spread that creates value, though narrow enough that competitive pressure could close it.

The business throws off $92M in free cash flow — roughly 28 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.05× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year.
Shareholder yield is only 2.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 4.6% of the shares.

sector_headwinds.text: Altman Z in the distress zone (0.2) — the kind of balance-sheet risk that can make a loss permanent
Low reinvestment-driven growth suggests the compounding engine has stalled
Insiders are net sellers (94% sell ratio, net $4.0M) — the people closest to the business are reducing their personal stake
Late-cycle dynamics increase the probability of a slowdown
Credit cycles and regulatory capital — losses accumulate invisibly in good years and appear all at once, and the time to worry is when underwriting standards are loosest.
Fintech disintermediation — neobanks, embedded finance, and blockchain rails are unbundling the fee streams that traditional banks took for granted.
Interest rate regime shifts — a rapid move in rates can invert the yield curve, crush bond portfolios, and trigger deposit flight simultaneously.

sector_tailwinds: Trading at a 60% margin of safety to estimated fair value — a real cushion against errors in the estimate
Market is pricing in lower growth than the company has historically delivered
Healthy payout ratio leaves room for both dividend growth and reinvestment
Minimal goodwill on the balance sheet — low impairment risk

mkt: The shares are in a strong uptrend, up 28% over the past year excluding the latest month.

With annualised volatility of 22% and a beta of 0.82, it moves roughly with the market, though its beta has shifted (1y 0.05 vs 5y 0.77), so read it loosely.

val: The stock trades 60% below its DCF fair value of $79.59, a meaningful margin of safety.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 35%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $60.98 to $107 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
Against its own history it is cheap: the EBIT multiple sits 15% below its 10-year median.
The 5 covering analysts target $37.05 on average, 15% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
The price implies 8.3% annual cash-flow growth, 20pp less than the model expects.
prof: ROIC of 17% clears the cost of capital of 8.9% by 8pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 0.35).
It converts 28% of revenue into free cash flow.
It earns a 10% return on equity.
Operating margin is running 6pp above its own historical average, a peak-margin risk if conditions normalise.
growth: Revenue has compounded at 12.4% over 3 years, 16.8% over 5 years and 24.1% over 10 years, so growth is decelerating, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 16%).
Net reinvestment is nil (capex and working capital no more than cover depreciation), so fundamental growth is near zero.
It has beaten earnings estimates by 6.4% on average.
Analysts expect 9.0% long-term annual earnings growth.
own: Insiders own a modest 4.6%, and institutions hold 60%.
Insider trading is two-way: 1 purchase and 17 sales over the past year, net $4.0M sold.
Shareholder yield is a modest 2.0% (0.4% in buybacks and 1.9% in dividends).
The share count has grown 7.7% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
people: With about 821 employees, each generates about $395K of revenue, 0.8x the Financial Services median, and productivity has risen 24.1% a year.
That works out to $112K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $1.5M (4x revenue per employee).
